Jobs for Psychology Majors

You don't have to have a Master's degree or doctoral degree to work in the field of Psychology.� To be a psychologist or psychiatrist, you do need degrees, but entry level jobs for psychology graduates are available.

Many entry level jobs in psychology use people skills.� For example, communication with and relating to people from diverse backgrounds is often required for case workers, sales, marketing personnel, and management positions.��

Analytical skills are useful because they give employees the necessary skills for problem solving.��

Writing skills are also useful for logically developed written reports and research which can involve using statistical tables and graphs to analyze problems and to communicate relevant findings.

A variety of work settings include human services (counselling, social work), business, criminal justice (probation officer, corrections officer), health and recreation, and education.




Although most people who go into the field of Psychology are usually intending to be a psychologist or psychiatrist, there are many entry level positions that can be filled without being one:


The types of jobs available if you have a Master's and/or PhD in Psychology are often in the following 2 areas: 1)Teaching and Research and, 2) Applied Work.

Teaching and Research

People who teach undergraduate, Master's level, or doctoral-level students usually work in a university setting. Most people who each at the university level are also involved in research.� If you do not want to teach and only want to focus on research, then you can work for various government agencies or private research organizations.� To work as a psychologist in any of these setting, you most likely will need a PhD in Psychology.� You might be able to get a job teaching psychology courses at a community college with a Master's degree in Psychology.
